### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/data-flow.mdx`  _(via OperationContext (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via OperationContext (symbol, a top-level interface))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **27** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fc6ddb87a4cd065171080f018cd865cd9c84c9d9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d9207719966eaa4c98352fa2c27770570af11181` — the merge of head `0474ea38f3626627a9052a0806b7d989c6cf08f9` into base `fc6ddb87a4cd065171080f018cd865cd9c84c9d9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d9207719966eaa4c98352fa2c27770570af11181 && git checkout d9207719966eaa4c98352fa2c27770570af11181
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fc6ddb87a4cd065171080f018cd865cd9c84c9d9 0474ea38f3626627a9052a0806b7d989c6cf08f9 && git checkout -B drift-repro fc6ddb87a4cd065171080f018cd865cd9c84c9d9 && git merge --no-ff 0474ea38f3626627a9052a0806b7d989c6cf08f9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fc6ddb87a4cd065171080f018cd865cd9c84c9d9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs fc6ddb87a4cd065171080f018cd865cd9c84c9d9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0474ea38f3626627a9052a0806b7d989c6cf08f9`

Read: card #19989 body and 5 comments (the two `os-dev-report` comments treated as claims), PR #20012 body, `git diff 1f05ea4fb2..0474ea38f3` (17 files, +823/-71; merge base = `1f05ea4fb2`, matches the gate's own "Diffing HEAD from 1f05ea4fb"), head blobs of `engine.ts`, `security-plugin.ts`, both foreign notes, the new note, `rls.zod.ts`, ADR-0058, `engine-update-dispatch.ts`, `check-empty-changeset.mjs`; Ruling D (#17712 comment 5660919394); `landing-operations.md` L15-16; `contract-review.md`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **By-id update judged on the stored row through `OperationContext.postHookWriteImageCheck` — RIGHT.** `engine.ts` head L13455-13461: on the `if (hookContext.input.id)` branch the seam runs after `assertNoStrictDrops()` (L13427) and before `evaluateValidationRules` (L13468) / `driver.update` (L13486). Above it: `priorRecord` read under the not-found gate (L12856-12886, so it is never null here), `triggerHooks('beforeUpdate')` (L12898), `encryptSecretFields` (L13242), `stripReadonlyWhenFields` (L13385), `stripReadonlyFields` (L13419). Image = `coerceBooleanFields(updateSchema, { ...priorRecord, ...hookContext.input.data })`, byte-for-byte the predicate path's per-row shape at L13709-13718. Nothing between the seam and the statement changes a value. Matches `RowLevelSecurityPolicySchema.check` ("matched against the new row") and ADR-0058 D4 (by-id path plus bulk path). The new test file drives this through the real `SecurityPlugin` + `ObjectQL` on two SQL drivers and reads rows off the driver table; the `qa_case` cell pins that the image carries a field the payload never sent.
- **Change-set-as-sent judgement kept; the change only refuses more — RIGHT.** `security-plugin.ts` head L3146-3160: the by-id `postImage = { ...pre, ...opCtx.data }` + `satisfiesCheck` block is textually unchanged apart from its comment. The seam installed at L3212-3213 is the same `newWriteImageCheck()` closure (same `checkParts`, same `denyCheck`). Every admission on base requires passing the middleware judgement; head requires that AND the seam. No path admits on head that refused on base: the falsy-id shape (next bullet) was already a 403. The "only refuses MORE" cell (org_b sent, stamp would land org_a, still refused) pins the kept judgement; ablation A3 as reported is consistent with that.
- **Falsy-payload-id refusal before `next()` — RIGHT.** Head L3174-3196: only when `targetId != null && !targetId` (`extractSingleId` returns the scalar `''`/`0`, L6419-6431) AND `resolveEngineUpdateDispatch(opCtx.data, opCtx.options).kind === 'by-id'` (metadata-core: a falsy payload id falls through to a truthy scalar `where.id`, L438-446). That is exactly the shape where the middleware's by-id gates judged the payload id while the engine writes the `where.id` row. On base this write reached the driver and was refused by the fail-closed guard afterwards (the seam was installed for `!targetId` and the engine took the by-id branch which never honoured it). Refusing earlier with nothing stored is strictly narrower. It sits inside the `checkParts.length > 0` block (L3064-3089), so it applies only where a `check` applies, which is the set the old guard covered. Predicate control (`multi: true`, no `where.id`) still routes to the seam. `resolveEngineUpdateDispatch` is exported from `@objectstack/metadata-core` (`index.ts` L38) and metadata-core is a declared runtime dependency of plugin-security. Refusal carries `PERMISSION_DENIED` on the shared `userFacingDenialMessage` copy.
- **Fail-closed guard now covers by-id updates — RIGHT.** The guard (L3579-3597) is unchanged code; its reach widens because `writeImageCheckSeam` is now set for every update (L3212). A host that executes a by-id update without honouring the seam gets 403 + `error` log, as inserts and predicate updates already did. Declared in the changeset under "Writes that are now refused". Pinned by the fail-closed cell.
- **Public doc comments on `OperationContext` — RIGHT.** `engine.ts` L2235-2258: the sentence "A by-id `update` is never handed to the seam" is replaced with the by-id call and its image; "called at most once per operation" still holds (one call per branch). Both statements match the code above. No public signature changes anywhere in the diff.
- **Test harness updates — RIGHT, with one bounded note.** Eight plugin-security engine doubles now run the seam on every update over `targets.map(r => ({ ...r, ...data }))` (`rls-check-membership-staging` moved from payload-only to merged, which is the real engine's shape); `check-only-write-scope` drops its `dispatch.kind === 'by-id' ? undefined : seam` exclusion. All go through `assertEngineUpdateDispatch`, the producer's own predicate. `security-plugin.test.ts` evaluates `[]` on updates: vacuous but not a false pin, because with no hooks the engine's image equals the middleware's image, so every admission there is one the engine gives too (documented in the file). `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sys-user-self-service-route.test.ts`: the terminal now runs the seam on `{ ...ROWS[id], ...opCtx.data }` via `assertEngineUpdateDispatch` from `@objectstack/objectql` (a declared devDependency; re-exported at `objectql/src/index.ts` L318), by-id only, without touching `preImageWheres`. Note: the harness runs the seam BEFORE the identity write guard, whereas the engine runs hooks before the seam; the only check this file composes reads `id`, which the guard never touches, so no verdict can differ, and Test Core (6/6) is green on this head. Nothing in any harness pins an outcome the real engine does not produce.

#### Deliberate correction

**Note 1: `.changeset/19950-rls-check-multi-row-writes.md`** (pending, foreign; base blob `8a18ab3971`, head blob `4f3fdb5bbf`), section "What does not change", first bullet.
- Base sentence: "A by-id update and a single-row insert are judged exactly as before."
- New sentence: "A single-row insert is judged exactly as before. A by-id update is not changed by this entry; its judgement on the row it stores is its own entry (#19989)."
- Base false in a release that ships this PR: YES. The compiled CHANGELOG reads "exactly as before" against the previous release; with #19989 in the same release a by-id update is judged on a second image it never was before. Ruling D's class applies.
- New sentence true on the head tree: YES. Insert is untouched by this diff (no insert code changes). The 19950 diff (#19988) did not change the by-id branch (base step 3.6 still read "BY-ID UPDATE — unchanged"), so "not changed by this entry" holds. `.changeset/19989-by-id-update-post-hook-check.md` exists at head and states the stored-row judgement.
- Byte proof: `diff -u` base vs head = one hunk, one `-` line, one `+` line, nothing else; word diff touches only that bullet.
- Citation: `#19989` GET 200.

**Note 2: `.changeset/insert-check-post-image.md`** (pending, foreign; base blob `33fd97c8e4`, head blob `1bc422f7b8`), paragraph "What changed, mechanically".
- Base clause: "`update` is unchanged."
- New clause: "this entry leaves `update` unchanged, and the predicate and by-id updates move onto the same seam in their own entries (#19950, #19989)."
- Base false in a release that ships this PR: YES. Unqualified "`update` is unchanged" in a release whose other two entries change both update shapes is false at release level (it was already strained by #19950; this PR finishes it).
- New clause true on the head tree: YES. `security-plugin.ts` still installs the insert seam unconditionally (L3138-3144, untouched); the predicate seam call is at `engine.ts` L13709 (#19950) and the by-id call at L13455 (#19989); both entries are present in `.changeset/` at head.
- Byte proof: `diff -u` base vs head = one hunk, one `-` line, one `+` line; word diff shows `{+this entry leaves+}` and the replaced tail only.
- Citations: `#19950` GET 200, `#19989` GET 200.

No third changeset on the merge base is touched (diff stat: exactly these two `M` rows plus the one `A` row).

### ② Semver level

RIGHT. `@objectstack/plugin-security` and `@objectstack/objectql` at `minor` are the two packages with source changes (metadata-core and plugin-auth carry only an import consumer and a test). `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is consistent across claim, PR body line 2 and changeset: the diff adds no export, key, or accepted call shape; `postHookWriteImageCheck` and `resolveEngineUpdateDispatch` pre-exist; every behaviour change is in the refusing direction (three listed, all verified above). `(narrowing)` is BREAKING per AGENTS.md, carried by the `!` headline and the BREAKING paragraph; `minor` for a breaking narrowing is the documented launch-window rule (`content/docs/protocol/backward-compatibility.mdx` L17, L114, L184-206; `check-changeset-no-major` refuses `major`), the same route 19950 took. The BREAKING paragraph is honest: it names the narrowing, the three refused shapes, the unchanged refusal code, and a remedy. `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is honest: `packages/spec` is untouched, no authorable key, spelling or stored shape moves, and the prescribed remedy is behavioural (hook, policy `check`, or data); the arm is one the gate's list accepts (`check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` L497). `Check Changeset` is the only changeset-family red and it is the foreign-note rule, not the no-major or registration rule.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` (domain:engine, another lane):** declared in the claim ("If the measured producer is the engine, the by-id branch of `update()` ... which the seat declares cross-seat"). The diff stays inside that declaration: the by-id branch seam call, the `OperationContext` doc comments for that seam, and a four-line comment on the predicate branch pointing at it. No other engine code moves. Answered: within the declared surface.
- **Expected `check-empty-changeset` red:** `Check Changeset` is the ONLY failure on this head (two check-run ids, 107791550960 and 107791947709, one job run on two events; both identical). Each carries exactly two file annotations, `.changeset/19950-rls-check-multi-row-writes.md` and `.changeset/insert-check-post-image.md`, "present on the merge base and CHANGED by this PR", with the DELIBERATE CORRECTION remedy text; the remaining annotations are the job's exit line and a runner-image notice. Nothing else is named. Other non-green at the final poll: `Auto Label` (one of two runs) skipped, `Check PR Size` (one of two runs) skipped, `Build Docs` skipped, `Console Pin Gate` skipped, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)` skipped — skips, not reds. Still in progress, reported as PENDING not failing: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Test Core (1/6)`, `Test Core (4/6)`, `Test Core (5/6)`, `Dogfood Regression Gate (2/3)`, `Dogfood Regression Gate (3/3)`. Green: Build Core, Test Core 2/6, 3/6, 6/6 (the plugin-auth shard that was red on `7efc9eb010`), all four Type Check jobs, Temporal Conformance, Dogfood 1/3, Dogfood Verify CLI, and the queue guards. Under landing-operations L15-16 this record confirms the by-design red; the pending jobs remain the enqueue condition ("PR check 全绿"), not this record's.
- **Not flagged by the implementer, for the seat:** (1) `packages/spec/src/security/rls.zod.ts` L432, the published `check` `.describe()`, still says "an array insert and a `multi: true` update are not post-image checked". False since #19988 merged; identical on the merge base and on `origin/main`, untouched by this PR (the claim forbids `packages/spec`). Spec-lane card, not a defect of this PR. (2) The plugin-auth harness's seam-before-guard ordering, bounded as stated in ①. (3) `Check Changeset` runs twice on this head; both runs must be read as the one by-design red. Implementer-flagged items (the step 3.7 Layer 0 by-id twin; the ADR-0095 D1 reading in the card's section 1) are correctly left unfixed and belong on their own cards.
